definitions.title: The Alternating Series Test (Leibniz's Theorem)
definitions.latex: \sum (-1)^{n-1} u_n \text{ converges if: } (1) \; u_{n+1} \le u_n \; \forall n, \quad \text{and } (2) \; \lim_{n \to \infty} u_n = 0
definitions.statement: An alternating series sum (-1)^(n-1) u_n with positive terms u_n converges if the terms decrease monotonically and approach zero.
definitions.explanation: Partial sums oscillate between upper and lower bounds that tighten around a single limit point.
definitions.keyTakeaway: Alternating signs + decreasing terms + terms -> 0 = Convergence.

definitions.title: Alternating Series Estimation Theorem
definitions.statement: If an alternating series satisfies the conditions of the Alternating Series Test, the truncation error R_n after n terms does not exceed the absolute value of the first unused term u_{n+1}.
definitions.explanation: Provides instant computable error bounds without needing improper integrals.
definitions.keyTakeaway: Truncation error is strictly bounded by the magnitude of the next term.
